Updated 2026-11-18 from analysis version `admission_age_elapsed_time_los_v2`. Generated from aggregate [current results](CURRENT_ANALYSIS.json).

## Executive summary

In 11,964 COPD ICU admissions, pre-ICU RAAS exposure was associated with lower observed in-hospital mortality hazard in the refined age/sex-adjusted, era-stratified Cox model (HR 0.732 (0.592–0.904); p=0.00383). The exploratory first-day-SOFA core specification had an attenuated estimate (HR 0.833 (0.673–1.030); p=0.09122). These estimates are observational associations and cannot establish a treatment effect.

## Data source and cohort

MIMIC-IV v3.1 admissions with the existing ICD-9/10 COPD definition were anchored to the first ICU stay within each hospital admission. Patients may contribute repeated admissions. Adult selection uses `anchor_age + admission_year - anchor_year >= 18`. The same admission-age estimate is preserved through baseline and outcome construction. `anchor_age=91` denotes an aggregated age group above 89 in the anchor year, so year adjustment does not recover an exact age.

| Characteristic | Overall | No RAAS | RAAS |

| First-day SOFA, median (IQR) | 4 (2–6) | 4 (2–7) | 4 (2–6) |

## Exposure, outcome, and methods

Exposure flags identify inpatient prescription records in the same hospital admission with `starttime <= intime`. They do not verify actual administration, continued treatment at ICU entry, adherence or concurrent ACEi/ARB administration. Both positive class flags mean qualifying records for both classes; they do not establish simultaneous treatment. Neither means no qualifying prescription record for either class, not proven absence of all medication use.

Follow-up begins at ICU admission and ends at recorded in-hospital death or live discharge. Discharge time is used for death only when death time is missing, with an explicit fallback flag. All intervals, including ICU and hospital LOS, are calculated from DATETIME microsecond differences divided by 86,400,000,000. Death/discharge timestamps, event values, positive follow-up, and downstream lineage are validated before analysis.

There were 2 fallback deaths. In the original main analysis, live discharge is censored and Cox intervals use ordinary admission-level inference without patient clustering or frailty. Supplementary patient-cluster and competing-event results are reported separately below. Primary 04a adjusts for age and sex and stratifies by anchor year group. Core 04c additionally adjusts for SOFA, CHF, CKD and diabetes. ICU sensitivity models add pooled ICU types; penalties remain 0.1 for core and 0.01 for ICU. Original unpooled ICU estimates are retained in the archived age/time audit.

## Timing of severity information

`sofa_score` comes from `mimiciv_3_1_derived.first_day_sofa`. Its published definition can use information through 24 hours after ICU entry, while follow-up starts at ICU entry. All SOFA-containing core, ICU-adjusted and CHF/SOFA-stratified models in the original ICU-entry workflow are therefore exploratory sensitivity analyses that can use post-start information, not baseline-only severity adjustment. Temporal leakage or adjustment for post-exposure information may affect interpretation; its impact has not been quantified here. The primary age/sex model with era strata is unchanged. A separate exploratory 24-hour landmark analysis is reported in the supplementary results; pre-ICU severity reconstruction remains unperformed.

[Published first-day SOFA definition](https://github.com/MIT-LCP/mimic-code/blob/main/mimic-iv/concepts/firstday/first_day_sofa.sql). The deployed derived-table definition and individual measurement times were not inspected in this documentation audit. [Separate reanalysis options](https://github.com/makotoy56/mimic-iv-copd-raas-analysis/blob/main/docs/ANALYSIS_TIMING_LIMITATIONS.md).

## Kaplan-Meier results

The two-group log-rank statistic was 8.207, p=0.00417. These are unadjusted survival estimates under live-discharge censoring, not competing-risk-adjusted hospital death probabilities.

![Current Kaplan-Meier estimates](assets/kaplan_meier_curve.png)

**How to read**

- The horizontal axis is elapsed days since ICU entry; the vertical axis is the unadjusted Kaplan–Meier survival estimate. Blue represents qualifying pre-ICU RAAS orders and orange represents no qualifying orders. Shading shows pointwise 95% confidence intervals.
- Live discharge is censored. Consequently, one minus this curve is not the observed cumulative probability of hospital death when discharge is a competing event; use the separate CIF figure for that question.

**What the results show**

- The overall two-group log-rank p-value is 0.00417. It compares the unadjusted survival experience over follow-up, rather than testing every plotted day or controlling for age, severity and other confounding.

**Interpretation limits**

- Wider intervals in the late tail indicate less precise estimates. Visual separation is an observational association and does not establish a medication benefit. The curve is not an adjusted Cox prediction.

## Primary and extended Cox results

| Specification | RAAS HR (95% CI) | p |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Initial 04a: era entered as covariate | 0.724 (0.586–0.894) | 0.00272 |
| Primary refined | 0.732 (0.592–0.904) | 0.00383 |
| Exploratory core (first-day SOFA) | 0.833 (0.673–1.030) | 0.09122 |
| Exploratory core + L2 (0.1) | 0.886 (0.766–1.025) | 0.10376 |
| Exploratory ICU adjusted | 0.958 (0.772–1.187) | 0.69262 |
| Exploratory ICU + L2 (0.01) | 0.910 (0.743–1.115) | 0.36324 |
| Core CHF/SOFA strata (exploratory) | 0.830 (0.666–1.034) | 0.09666 |
| ICU CHF/SOFA/type strata (exploratory) | 1.127 (0.880–1.443) | 0.34395 |

![Exploratory core Cox estimates using first-day SOFA](assets/cox_forest_plot.png)

**How to read**

- Each dot is an adjusted hazard ratio; its horizontal bar is an ordinary admission-level 95% confidence interval. Colors distinguish covariate rows, not statistical significance. The dashed line at HR=1 represents equal hazards under the fitted model. The horizontal scale is linear.
- Read the unit of each row: age is per year, SOFA is per point, male sex is relative to female sex, and the binary RAAS/CHF/CKD/diabetes rows compare flag 1 with flag 0. Different units mean that distance from 1 cannot be used to rank clinical importance across rows.

**What the results show**

- The RAAS row is HR 0.833 (95% CI 0.673–1.030) in the era-stratified, unpenalized SOFA-core model. Its interval includes 1, so it does not establish a clear association in this specification; it does not prove equal hazards or no association.

**Interpretation limits**

- This is the exploratory 04c model, not the refined primary 04a model or the separate patient-cluster analysis. First-day SOFA may include post-start information. The estimates are conditional associations and cannot establish treatment effects.

![Current sensitivity comparison](assets/cox_model_sensitivity_comparison.svg)

**How to read**

- Every row estimates the same qualifying-RAAS-orders versus no-qualifying-orders contrast under a different Cox specification. Dots are HRs and horizontal bars are that specification's original 95% intervals on a linear scale. Colors separate model rows for readability; these are not different medication groups.

**What the results show**

- The primary estimate is 0.732 (95% CI 0.592–0.904); the exploratory SOFA-core estimate is 0.833 (95% CI 0.673–1.030). The results depend on the specification, and several intervals include HR=1. These plotted intervals use the original inference, not the later patient-cluster intervals or 24-hour landmark population.

**Interpretation limits**

- L2 rows use penalization; the ICU and PH-stratified rows change covariates or baseline-hazard strata. Their differences cannot isolate a single confounder, and one interval crossing 1 while another does not is not a test of the difference between estimates.
- SOFA-containing rows are exploratory and can use post-start information. The set of models is a sensitivity analysis of an observational association, not independent replications of a causal treatment effect.

All SOFA-containing rows and plots are exploratory sensitivity analyses with possible post-start information; their differences do not isolate baseline confounding.

## Subclass comparison

The ACEi-only-order, ARB-only-order and neither-order analysis includes 11,951 admissions. Its global three-group log-rank statistic is 9.124, p=0.01044. Records with both class flags positive are excluded. Each coefficient compares a subclass with neither qualifying order.

ACEi-only and ARB-only prescription-order groups are each compared with neither qualifying order. Records with both class flags positive are excluded from this subclass analysis. The main analysis reports no direct ACEi-versus-ARB contrast or interaction test. Different point estimates, or one p-value below 0.05 and the other above it, do not establish a difference between the classes.

![ACEi-only and ARB-only prescription orders, each versus neither](assets/raas_subgroup_forest_plot.svg)

**How to read**

- Both rows use neither qualifying order as the reference. The blue dot is ACEi-only and the orange dot is ARB-only. Each is an age/sex-adjusted, era-stratified HR with an ordinary admission-level 95% interval on a linear scale. HR=1 is the reference line; records with both class flags positive are excluded.

**What the results show**

- ACEi-only orders: 0.683 (95% CI 0.521–0.894); ARB-only orders: 0.805 (95% CI 0.573–1.131). The ACEi interval lies below 1, whereas the ARB interval includes 1.

**Interpretation limits**

- Different point estimates or p-value thresholds do not establish a difference between classes. This plot contains no direct ACEi-versus-ARB contrast and does not establish superiority or equivalence.
- The flags describe prescription orders, not verified administration or adherence. These associations do not estimate causal drug effects.

## PH diagnostics and interpretation

Primary refined rank PH p-values: age 0.79803, sex 0.32498, RAAS 0.72064. Core and ICU models still require diagnostic interpretation. The current results summary lists rank PH tests with p<0.05 and model warnings. Complete covariate-level rank PH p-values are saved in CURRENT_ANALYSIS.json. Exploratory CHF/SOFA-stratified models allow different baseline hazards; they supplement the primary model rather than redefine it.

See the [diagnostic summary and limitations](https://github.com/makotoy56/mimic-iv-copd-raas-analysis/blob/main/docs/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md#diagnostics-and-interpretation) for flagged tests, model warnings, sparse-strata limitations and rare-category pooling. Complete covariate-level rank PH p-values are available in [the aggregate analysis record](CURRENT_ANALYSIS.json), under each model’s `ph_rank_p` field. The approach follows [lifelines documentation on stratification](https://lifelines.readthedocs.io/en/latest/jupyter_notebooks/Proportional%20hazard%20assumption.html#Stratification). A non-significant diagnostic does not prove PH, and additional stratification changes the adjustment structure.

## Supplementary Sensitivity Analyses {#supplementary-sensitivity-analyses}

These post hoc analyses were added after the main analysis. They use the same corrected cohort and prescription-order exposure definition; the original main estimates remain unchanged. The [selected aggregate results](SURVIVAL_SENSITIVITY_RESULTS.json) are bound to the main reference and verified local run by hashes. Full methods and notebook links are in the [supplement guide](https://github.com/makotoy56/mimic-iv-copd-raas-analysis/blob/main/docs/SURVIVAL_SENSITIVITY_SUPPLEMENTS.md).

### Patient-cluster inference

The 11,964 admissions represent 9,157 patients; 1,656 patients contributed 4,463 admissions across repeated hospitalizations. Unpenalized age/sex/era and SOFA-core Cox models retain their original complete cases, covariates and Efron ties. Patient-level HC0 sandwich inference sums tie-aware scores across all admissions of each patient. Point estimates are shared by the two variance methods; intervals and two-sided normal Wald p-values can change. No finite-cluster correction or frailty model is used.

| Specification | HR | Ordinary 95% CI | Patient-cluster 95% CI | Cluster p |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| Primary age/sex/era | 0.732 | 0.592–0.904 | 0.593–0.902 | 0.00346 |
| Exploratory first-day-SOFA core | 0.833 | 0.673–1.030 | 0.665–1.042 | 0.11019 |

The primary interval changes little. The SOFA-core cluster interval includes HR=1; this does not establish equivalence or eliminate residual confounding.

### Death and live discharge as competing events

A two-cause Aalen-Johansen estimate treats recorded in-hospital death and live discharge as competing endpoints. Curves are unadjusted admission-level cumulative incidence through day 28. Pointwise 95% percentile intervals use 1,000 patient-cluster bootstrap samples, carrying all admissions and exposure groups of each sampled patient together, with fixed patient ordering and seed 20261118. Tied endpoints use a shared pre-event risk set without jitter. The original discharge-time proxy is retained for the two deaths with missing death timestamps. These intervals are not simultaneous confidence bands.

| Qualifying RAAS orders | Day | Death CIF %, 95% CI | Live-discharge CIF %, 95% CI |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| No | 7 | 8.90 (8.41–9.43) | 43.62 (42.66–44.59) |
| No | 14 | 11.84 (11.26–12.42) | 69.55 (68.68–70.48) |
| No | 28 | 13.90 (13.28–14.54) | 81.68 (80.95–82.40) |
| Yes | 7 | 5.60 (4.15–7.15) | 49.58 (46.34–52.83) |
| Yes | 14 | 8.03 (6.21–9.93) | 77.70 (74.73–80.39) |
| Yes | 28 | 9.09 (7.09–11.08) | 87.95 (85.76–90.06) |

At day 28, the unadjusted death-CIF difference (qualifying RAAS orders minus no qualifying orders) was -4.81 percentage points (95% CI -6.82 to -2.66). This is an unadjusted association, not a treatment effect.

![Unadjusted death and live-discharge cumulative incidence; shaded areas are pointwise patient-bootstrap 95% intervals. Panels use different vertical scales.](assets/supplementary_competing_risks.svg){fig-alt="Two panels show unadjusted cumulative incidence of death and live discharge through day 28, by qualifying RAAS prescription orders, with pointwise bootstrap intervals."}

**How to read**

- The horizontal axis is days since ICU entry. The left panel is the unadjusted cumulative incidence of hospital death and the right panel is live discharge, treating the other endpoint as competing. Blue denotes qualifying RAAS orders; orange denotes no qualifying orders. Each curve's height is an absolute cumulative probability, not a hazard ratio.
- Shading shows pointwise patient-bootstrap 95% intervals on the saved daily grid. These are not simultaneous confidence bands. The published death panel spans 0–20%, while the discharge panel spans 0–100%; compare the printed percentages rather than line heights between panels.

**What the results show**

- At day 28, death CIF is 9.09% with qualifying orders and 13.90% without. Live-discharge CIF is 87.95% and 81.68%, respectively. The saved estimates indicate different observed endpoint patterns between the groups.

**Interpretation limits**

- These curves are unadjusted associations and do not establish a treatment effect. They answer a different question from the adjusted cause-specific HRs and from Kaplan–Meier curves that censor discharge. No Fine–Gray model is shown.

Separate age/sex/era cause-specific Cox models describe rates among admissions still alive and hospitalized. The death HR equals the clustered primary estimate above. The live-discharge HR was 1.168 (patient-cluster 95% CI 1.087–1.254; p=0.00002). These adjusted hazard ratios and the unadjusted CIFs answer different questions. No Fine–Gray model is reported.

### A separate 24-hour severity landmark

Follow-up starts 24 hours after the original ICU entry among admissions alive and still hospitalized beyond that point. Exclusions were 254 deaths and 178 live discharges at or before 24 hours, plus 2 remaining deaths with unknown death times. This left 11,530 eligible admissions; 0 had missing core covariates. Both models use the same complete cases, unchanged pre-ICU prescription-order classification, era strata, and patient-cluster Efron inference; one day is subtracted from eligible follow-up.

| Landmark specification | Admissions | Deaths | HR | Patient-cluster 95% CI | p |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Age/sex/era | 11,530 | 1,436 | 0.771 | 0.617–0.965 | 0.02313 |
| Exploratory first-day-SOFA core | 11,530 | 1,436 | 0.854 | 0.673–1.082 | 0.19133 |

This is a conditional analysis with a different population and time origin. It relies on the published first-day-SOFA definition through ICU entry plus one day; deployed component windows and individual measurement times have not been independently reconstructed. First-day severity follows exposure and may mediate associations or induce selection/collider bias. Comorbidity-code timing is unchanged. Differences from the ICU-entry analysis cannot isolate baseline severity adjustment. Pre-ICU severity reconstruction remains unperformed.

### Validation and interpretation

Ordinary estimates were checked against the saved main reference before these results were saved. Synthetic tied and untied calculations matched R survival for Cox coefficients, ordinary and patient-cluster covariance, and Aalen-Johansen probabilities. That synthetic comparison is not an independent clinical refit of these clustered estimates. The [supplement validation record](SURVIVAL_SUPPLEMENTS_VALIDATION.json) documents the checks and remaining limitations. All three analyses are reported regardless of significance; none establishes a causal treatment effect.

## Reproducibility checks

Six unpenalized Cox specifications (40 coefficients) were independently recalculated with statsmodels PHReg using matched complete cases, era/additional strata and Efron ties. Coefficients, HRs, confidence-interval endpoints and p-values matched the lifelines reference within an absolute tolerance of 1e-4. The saved comparison is bound to this exact aggregate analysis snapshot by its reference hash. See [the calculation record](INDEPENDENT_COX_CROSSCHECK.json) and [the scope and limitations](https://github.com/makotoy56/mimic-iv-copd-raas-analysis/blob/main/docs/INDEPENDENT_REVALIDATION.md).

This checks a separate statistical implementation on the same corrected model inputs. Source-SQL extraction is evaluated separately. Penalized fits, PH diagnostics, patient clustering, competing risks and causal validity are not established by this numerical comparison.

The reproducible workflow covers authorized MIMIC source access, version-controlled BigQuery extraction and cohort construction, explicit model-column retrieval, Python modeling, independent numerical comparison, figure generation and Quarto reporting. Only aggregate results are published; no external analysis-service upload is part of this workflow. See [the full reproduction steps](https://github.com/makotoy56/mimic-iv-copd-raas-analysis/blob/main/REPRODUCIBILITY.md).

## Limitations

These findings cannot establish causality. Confounding by indication, unmeasured severity, exposure misclassification and a single health system limit interpretation. Age is approximate, especially in the aggregated oldest group. The original main estimates retain ordinary admission-level inference and discharge censoring; supplementary analyses report patient-cluster inference and competing-event cumulative incidence. Rare ICU pooling and PH-responsive strata remain exploratory sensitivity choices. First-day SOFA may include post-start information; these models do not isolate baseline confounding. No direct between-class contrast or verified medication-administration comparison is reported.
